messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff & timeline options — Elm Street Health

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned after the discovery: 

1) High-level recap (what we heard)
- Primary use case: clinician-facing summarization + embedding search for care pathways.
- Traffic profile: steady daytime load with spikes at midnight ET for batch jobs.
- Key constraints: PHI handling, on-prem option for audit logs, and predictable latency SLOs.

2) Draft Mutual Action Plan (attached) — what’s included:
- Milestones (Discovery → Pilot → Security Review → Procurement → GA deployment) with ownership and target dates.
- Dependencies (security questionnaire, SOC2 evidence, procurement review, infra staging).
- Decision gate criteria for pilot -> GA.

3) Proposed timeline options (pick one):
A) Accelerated (6 weeks): Discovery (1 week), Pilot (3 weeks), Security + Procurement parallel (2 weeks); target close: 2026-05-28. Requires expedited security responses and procurement prioritization.
B) Standard (10 weeks): Discovery (2), Pilot (4), Security (2), Procurement (2) — target close: 2026-06-30. More conservative, gives your teams breathing room.

Ask: Please confirm (a) which timeline you prefer, (b) key stakeholders we should add to the MAP (procurement, security, platform owner), and (c) target close date you’d like us to aim for.

I attached an initial MAP workbook (Redwood_MAP_Kickoff_v1.xlsx) with milestone owners filled based on today’s call. Marissa will lead the security questionnaire work from our side; Monica will be your technical SE for the pilot.

If useful I can convert the MAP to a shared Google Sheet and drop links to the SOC2 artifacts we referenced.

Thanks — talk soon,

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Thanks, Karthik — good summary. A couple of quick points: 

- Stakeholders to include:
  * Maya Patel (Procurement) — maya.patel@elmstreethealth.com
  * Ellen Barnes (CTO) — ellen.barnes@elmstreethealth.com
  * Security: I’ll loop in our CIS lead after I confirm availability.

- Timeline preference: We prefer the Standard (10 weeks) timeline. Target close: aiming for a June 30th decision, but procurement will likely push for a 2–3 week review window after pilot.

- Procurement asks: Please include a procurement milestone to capture contract review + redlines. We will want standard BAA language and an estimated cost breakdown by month for committed capacity.

Also, could you attach a version of the MAP that includes a single-column "Procurement owner / contact" and a separate sheet for security artifacts? That’ll make internal routing easier.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

— Alex
